object_description: angular four-storey building with a pronounced head formation
design_condition: The building completes the existing development, maintains the surrounding scale, and shapes a spacious inner courtyard linked to the neighbourhood through a covered entrance passage.

positive.statement: The building fits well into its context and convincingly marks the entrance with a distinct head formation.

position.rationale: Distinct taller mass marks the entrance at the south-west edge in plan and south elevation.

positive.statement: The form and placement generate a spacious courtyard and a strong connection between school and neighbourhood space.

position.rationale: Open courtyard occupies the lower-left interior edge and connects toward the south.

positive.statement: The courtyard offers atmosphere and sufficient scope for everyday school life and public use.

position.rationale: Courtyard void is clearly legible in the top view at ground level.

positive.statement: The facade is carefully designed and responds skilfully to the unequal surrounding situations through differentiated mesh sizes.

position.rationale: South and east elevations show differing point densities across the articulated envelope.

positive.statement: The entrance hall is generous, flexible, and enlivens the urban space convincingly.

position.rationale: Interior hall is approximated behind the covered south entrance passage.

positive.statement: The learning landscape, roof garden, and classroom zoning function well together.

position.target: learning landscape, roof garden, and classroom zoning
position.rationale: Upper roof and articulated building mass provide the closest exterior anchor for these internal functions.

positive.statement: The clear organization and distribution of rooms provide high utility value and support school operations positively.

position.rationale: Internal layout is represented by a distributed approximation across the building envelope.

positive.statement: The supporting structure has a clear concept and is carefully planned for straightforward implementation.

position.rationale: Structure is not separately visible, so it is anchored to the west structural envelope.

negative.statement: The tree requires native soil to develop a spatially effective crown appropriate to its species.

position.rationale: Tree is not distinguishable; courtyard ground provides the most plausible landscape anchor.

negative.statement: Statements about railings and technical structures, especially in the roof area, are missing.

position.rationale: Roof area is visible, but railings and technical equipment are not separately identifiable.

negative.statement: The escape route above the gymnasium must be solved differently.

position.rationale: The route is constrained to an elevated south-side building surface; gymnasium location is indistinct.

negative.statement: The arrangement of fitness and gymnastics in the unexposed basement is unsatisfactory.

position.rationale: Basement functions are not visible, so the lower building envelope supplies a distributed ground-level anchor.

negative.statement: The ventilation concept for the rooms is unresolved.

position.rationale: Ventilation is unresolved internally and is approximated across the eastern building envelope.

negative.statement: The large basement, extensive roof garden, window proportion, and sun protection have a negative impact on life-cycle costs.

position.rationale: This is primarily a whole-building economic judgment spanning several components.

negative.statement: The transition between the ground and basement structures and the canopy anchoring still require coordination.

position.rationale: Lower south edge and entrance canopy provide the closest visible coordination location.
